summary: MODEL_CHANGE_REQUIRED: the update moves learner logging of DIFF-synced proposals before the NEWLEADER ACK but does not wait for their fsync. Model, harness and traces were updated; model checking found a CommittedQuorumDurable counterexample that was reproduced on the updated implementation (a transaction served by the leader is lost after the acking learners crash). Two further update-introduced defects were reproduced from code review.
validation_limits: All TLC campaigns are finite-bound: canonical MC/base runs are exhaustive only up to the inherited level-23 state constraint; the full update BFS stopped at its CommittedQuorumDurable counterexample, focused/open/discharge BFS runs stopped at their 30-minute budget (on a superset transition relation) and were followed by 30-minute simulations on the final model (LIMITED_COVERAGE, not proofs).
The stale data-tree election vote of CR-2 is not represented in the model (votes use durable history); it is evidenced by a real trace only.
CR-3 (proposal ACK consumed as NEWLEADER ACK) is a liveness/availability issue outside the safety model; confirmed only by reproduction.
The MC-1 reproduction uses a test-fixture fsync hold (slow disk) and SIGKILL-equivalent data-directory images; without a slow disk the window was not hit in 3 natural-timing runs.
JDK 21 / in-process multi-server JUnit environment, as in the prior run.

findings.title: NEWLEADER ACK is sent before the DIFF-synced transactions are durable
findings.cause: Learner.syncWithLeader (NEWLEADER) only enqueues the buffered sync proposals to the asynchronous SyncRequestProcessor via FollowerZooKeeperServer.logRequest and then writes the NEWLEADER ACK; the leader counts that ACK toward the quorum that makes it commit and serve its whole loaded history.
findings.trigger: A transaction durable only on the re-elected leader is transferred by DIFF; the learners ACK NEWLEADER, the leader starts serving it, and the acking learners crash before their SyncRequestProcessor fsync while the old leader is unavailable.
findings.consequence: A new leader is elected without the transaction that clients already read, and the old leader's only copy is truncated when it rejoins (lost committed write).

premises: The learner writes the NEWLEADER ACK without waiting for the SyncRequestProcessor flush of the proposals it just logged.
The leader activates on a NEWLEADER ACK quorum and serves its whole loaded history.
Learner process crashes (or power loss) can happen between the ACK and the asynchronous fsync.

findings.title: Learner failure between NEWLEADER and UPTODATE leaks an INITIAL ZooKeeperServer
findings.cause: The update starts the learner's request processors at NEWLEADER with startupWithoutServing (state INITIAL), but ZooKeeperServer/LearnerZooKeeperServer.shutdown skip a server that is not RUNNING or ERROR, so a learner that fails before UPTODATE never stops those processors or fast-forwards its data tree.
findings.trigger: A learner fails (e.g. read timeout) after handling NEWLEADER and before startServing, then re-joins.
findings.consequence: Each failed sync leaks the abandoned server's processor threads (3 failures left 3 extra CommitProcessor threads; none on the old revision); the leaked SyncThread keeps writing the shared log after the peer left the session and the peer's election vote uses a data tree older than its durable log (observed in a real trace).

premises: startupWithoutServing leaves the server INITIAL until startServing after UPTODATE.
canShutdown() accepts only RUNNING and ERROR.

findings.title: A proposal ACK can be consumed as the NEWLEADER ACK
findings.cause: The SyncRequestProcessor started at NEWLEADER can write a proposal ACK before the learner thread writes the NEWLEADER ACK; LearnerHandler treats the first ACK after NEWLEADER as the NEWLEADER ACK and waitForNewLeaderAck drops a mismatched zxid without counting the learner.
findings.trigger: Learners DIFF-sync a proposal from a new leader and their learner thread is delayed before writing the NEWLEADER ACK.
findings.consequence: The leader misses its NEWLEADER quorum although every learner acked; activation waited for a learner sync timeout and re-sync (about 22 s versus under 4 s on the old revision).

premises: LearnerHandler consumes the first packet after NEWLEADER as the NEWLEADER ACK.
Learner-side SyncRequestProcessor ACKs share the learner socket and are not ordered after the NEWLEADER ACK.
